humanities_role_explanation: The task is iconographic classification of Christian saints using Iconclass, a core art-historical operation (identifying subject matter per Panofsky). The benchmark targets disciplinary competence in iconography for metadata curation, though at the level of identification of a saint rather than deeper interpretation.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Paintings of Christian saints are paired with text prompts listing class labels (Test 1) or Iconclass descriptions (Test 2); few-shot adds exemplar images with labels. Model outputs are text labels.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Single-label classification of paintings into 10 Christian saint classes (Iconclass codes), under zero-shot with labels, zero-shot with Iconclass descriptions, and few-shot with five exemplars. It is essentially recognition of the depicted saint via attributes, not hermeneutic interpretation.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to a single task: single-label classification of Christian saints.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Flash, plus CLIP and SigLIP variants.

summary: The paper benchmarks CLIP, SigLIP, GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 models on single-label classification of Christian saints across three Iconclass-supporting datasets (ArtDL, ICONCLASS AI Test Set, Wikidata). It compares labels only, Iconclass descriptions, and few-shot exemplars against fine-tuned ResNet50 baselines. Multimodal LLMs beat the baselines on ArtDL and ICONCLASS but not on Wikidata.
key_findings: Gemini 2.5 Pro reached 90.45% on ArtDL and beat the ResNet50 baseline (84.44%). On Wikidata SigLIP-so400m was best (66.29%) and LLMs were around 45%. Descriptions generally helped zero-shot; few-shot mostly lowered accuracy. Cross-dataset consistency was low for LLMs (25-33%).
gold_upstream: ArtDL (Milani and Fraternali) and the Iconclass AI Test Set (Posthumus); Wikidata Iconclass statements. Each image is annotated with Iconclass codes; production not described in this paper.
facets_explanation: Labels come from Iconclass codes already attached to ArtDL, the ICONCLASS AI Test Set and Wikidata; the authors only filtered to the top-10 classes and removed multi-saint images. The paper does not describe how those annotations were produced. Identifying a saint from attributes requires external iconographic knowledge, and each image has one label.
results_explanation: Best score is gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06 on ArtDL Test 1, 90.45% accuracy; this is computed on the ArtDL test set of 1,864 images, whereas ICONCLASS (863 images) and Wikidata (718 images) are scored on different sets, so dataset_size 3445 is 1,864 + 863 + 718 (ArtDL counted by its test set only). The largest input-condition gap, recomputed across Tables 2-4 (Test 1 vs 2, Test 2 vs 3, zero-shot vs few-shot), is siglip-base-patch16-512 on ArtDL, 48.71% (labels) vs 68.19% (descriptions) = 19.48, reported as 19. Next largest: siglip-large ArtDL Test 2 72.21 vs Test 3 53.49 = 18.72; siglip-large Wikidata Test 3 61.17 vs Test 2 43.95 = 17.22. No human baseline is reported.
